meta.scalability_note: 40+ regions globally including EU, North America, APAC; managed auto-scaling via Instance Groups; up to 224 vCPUs (r3-960); global Anycast network
meta.performance_note: 99.99% availability SLA for key managed services; anti-DDoS VAC infrastructure protecting all services; multiple AZs per region; 17 Tbps network capacity

AWS Amplify.note: Managed shared and cloud web hosting available. Less developer-focused than Amplify (no built-in CI/CD, auth, or GraphQL).

AWS Lambda.note: Managed FaaS available (beta/early access). Supports Node.js, Python, Go. Less mature ecosystem than AWS Lambda.

Amazon ECS.note: Full container workload management via Managed Kubernetes. Docker-native workloads fully supported.

Amazon EKS.note: Fully managed Kubernetes clusters with automated upgrades and multi-AZ node pools.

Amazon EC2.note: Wide range of instance families: compute, memory, GPU, storage-optimised. Up to 224 vCPUs.

AWS Batch.note: Spot instances available for cost-effective batch workloads. No native managed batch service; requires orchestration tooling.

AWS Elastic Beanstalk.note: No managed PaaS deployment platform equivalent.

Amazon S3.note: S3-compatible object storage across EU regions. Standard and High Performance tiers.

Amazon S3 Glacier.note: Dedicated cold archival storage tier with tape-based backend. WORM compliance option available.

Amazon EBS.note: Persistent SSD block volumes attachable to instances. Classic and High Speed tiers.

AWS Backup.note: Automated and manual instance snapshots and volume backups. Backup policies configurable.

Amazon EFS.note: Managed NFS-based storage via NAS-HA product. Less elastic than AWS EFS; requires pre-provisioning capacity.

Amazon RDS.note: Fully managed PostgreSQL and MySQL with automated backups, high-availability, and read replicas.

Amazon DocumentDB.note: Managed MongoDB available (as part of the DBaaS portfolio). Not fully MongoDB-compatible on all APIs.

Amazon DynamoDB.note: No managed serverless key-value NoSQL database equivalent to DynamoDB.

Amazon Timestream.note: No managed time-series database. InfluxDB or TimescaleDB can be self-hosted.

Amazon Aurora.note: No Aurora-equivalent high-performance MySQL/PostgreSQL compatible engine.

Amazon ElastiCache.note: Fully managed Redis with clustering, replication and persistence options.

Amazon Redshift.note: Managed OpenSearch for analytics use cases. No columnar data warehouse equivalent to Redshift.

AWS Application Load Balancer.note: Managed HTTP/HTTPS load balancer with SSL termination, path-based routing, and health checks.

AWS Network Load Balancer.note: TCP/UDP layer-4 load balancing supported in the same managed product.

Amazon VPC.note: Private VLAN-based networking across OVHcloud services (vRack). Isolated private subnets fully supported.

Amazon Route 53.note: Managed DNS with Anycast infrastructure. Supports advanced records, TTL control, and zone management.

Amazon API Gateway.note: API Gateway product available in early access. REST API management with authentication and rate limiting.

Amazon CloudFront.note: Managed CDN available across OVHcloud edge locations. Integrates with Object Storage and Web Hosting.

AWS Direct Connect.note: Dedicated private connectivity (1–10 Gbps) between customer infrastructure and OVHcloud via partner PoPs.

Amazon Rekognition.note: No managed computer vision or image recognition API service.

Amazon SageMaker.equivalent: OVHcloud AI Notebooks / AI Training / AI Deploy
Amazon SageMaker.note: Managed Jupyter notebooks, training jobs, and model deployment. Less integrated than SageMaker; no AutoML or managed pipelines.

Amazon Bedrock.note: No managed Generative AI / foundation model API service.

AWS Glue.note: No managed serverless ETL/data pipeline service.

Amazon EMR.note: Managed Apache Spark job execution available. Limited to Spark; no Hadoop, Hive, or Presto managed services.

Amazon Athena.note: No serverless SQL query service over object storage.

AWS IAM.note: Policy-based IAM with users, groups, and service accounts. Supports fine-grained resource permissions.

Amazon Cognito.note: No dedicated app-level user authentication service. IAM covers account-level users only.

AWS IAM Identity Center.note: SAML-based SSO available for OVHcloud console. Limited to console access; no cross-service SSO like AWS IAM Identity Center.

AWS KMS.note: Managed KMS for key generation and encryption, integrated with Object Storage and Block Storage.

AWS Secrets Manager.note: Managed secret storage available in early access. API-accessible secrets with rotation support planned.

AWS Certificate Manager.note: Free Let's Encrypt and paid SSL certificates managed via OVHcloud. Auto-renewal available via ACME protocol.

Amazon GuardDuty.note: Advanced anti-DDoS (VAC) protecting all services. No ML-based threat detection comparable to GuardDuty.

AWS Security Hub.note: No centralised security findings aggregation or compliance dashboard.

AWS Config.note: No managed resource configuration compliance and drift detection service.

AWS Shield.note: Industry-leading anti-DDoS infrastructure (17 Tbps mitigation capacity) protecting all OVHcloud services at no extra cost.

AWS WAF.note: Managed WAF available with CDN and Load Balancer products. OWASP rule sets supported.

AWS CloudTrail.equivalent: OVHcloud Logs Data Platform / API audit
AWS CloudTrail.note: API call logs available. Logs Data Platform provides log streaming. Not as comprehensive as CloudTrail for cross-service audit.

Amazon CloudWatch.note: Separate metrics (Gra1) and logging (Logs Data Platform) products. Good observability but less unified than CloudWatch.

Amazon SNS.note: Basic alerting and webhook notifications available. No managed pub/sub notification service at the scale of SNS.

AWS Systems Manager.note: Server management tools available but no unified SSM-equivalent with patch management, parameter store, and OpsCenter.

AWS Cost Explorer.note: Detailed billing and cost breakdown per project and service available in the OVHcloud control panel.

Amazon ECR.note: Fully managed Harbor-based container registry with vulnerability scanning and multi-user access.

AWS CloudFormation.note: No native IaC service. Official OVHcloud Terraform provider available and well-maintained.

AWS IoT Core.note: Basic IoT connectivity features available. No full managed MQTT broker at the scale or feature set of AWS IoT Core.

AWS IoT Device Management.note: No managed IoT device registry or fleet management service.

Amazon SQS.note: Managed message queuing (Kafka-based / SQS-compatible API). Available across EU regions.

Amazon EventBridge.note: No managed event routing or serverless event bus service.

Amazon SES.note: Managed transactional and bulk email sending service. SMTP and API access.

Amazon Kinesis.note: No managed real-time data streaming service.
